newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuance to shift into high gear.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuance to shift into high gear.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity is expected to shift into high gear as players return from their holiday and names begin to emerge, dealers said.
"It's going to be a busy week," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Players are in the process of getting their deals together so it's just a matter of time."
On Tuesday, Wachovia Corp lead the way pricing $200 million in 10-year notes to yield 42 basis points over U.S. Treasuries via Smith Barney.
U.S. credit markets were closed on Monday in observance of the Veteran's Day holiday.
Also, Bristol Meyers priced $350 million in AAA-rated 30-year debentures to yield 34 basis over Treasuries via Goldman Sachs & Co, syndicate sources said.
Travelers/Aetna also tapped the market with $150 million in 10-year notes to yield 55 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Meanwhile, more names continue to trickle in as issuers get set to launch a slew of new deals, syndicate sources said.
ABN-Amro is expected to tap the market with $300 million in 30-year debt with a call option in the 10th year, sources said.
A recent drop in U.S. Treasury yields has spurred a flood of new issues as U.S. corporations lured by lower financing rates jump on the new issue bandwagon.
Currently, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 12/32 at 100-9/32 to yield 6.48 percent, its lowest level since early spring.
Other deals expected to price on Tuesday are ABN-Amro's $300 million 30-year debt offering which is expected to carry a call option in the 10th year, sources said.
ITT Corp is also expected to issue $250 million in seven-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, sources added.
Turning to the private placemnet arena, another $1.0 billion in 144A debt offerings are expected to come hit the market this week, sources said.
Celestica International is expected to issue $150 million in 144A senior subordianted guaranteed notes.
Blue Bird Body is expected to price $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Merrill Lynch. Price talk on the isuse is seen at 10.75 to 11.0 percent, dealers said.
Another $200 million is expected to come to market from Dollar Financial and Atrium Cos, which are each expected to bring $100 million in 144A issues, dealers added.
Cole National Corp is also expected to price $140 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via CIBC Wood Gundy.
In addition, IMED Corp may price $175 million 144A senior subordinatee notes due 2006 via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
The benchmark 30-year bond was quoted down 15/32 to 101-1/4 to yield 6.65 percent at 1028 EST/1528 GMT.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
